news app¶

The single Django app that implements the news site. Each section below is generated by Sphinx’s autodoc extension reading the module’s own docstrings.

Data models¶

Database models for The Daily Brief news application.

Defines the tables the app runs on and, more importantly, the rules that keep their data consistent. Validation lives in clean() and save() rather than only in forms, so the constraints hold however a row is written - admin dashboard, web form, API request or the shell.

class Publisher(*args, **kwargs)¶

Bases: Model

A news organisation that employs editors and journalists.

Editors and journalists are separate many-to-many relations rather than one combined list, because a person may work for several publishers and the two roles must stay distinguishable when deciding who may approve an article.

class User(*args, **kwargs)¶

Bases: AbstractUser

The project’s user account, extended with a news-app role.

Subclassing AbstractUser is what lets AUTH_USER_MODEL point here. It is also why every relation to a user references settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL instead of importing User - Django needs that indirection to resolve the swapped model.

class Role(*values)¶

The three roles an account can hold.

READER is the default, so a freshly registered account can neither publish nor approve until someone promotes it.

save(*args, **kwargs)¶

Save the account, then remove subscriptions it should not hold.

Only readers subscribe. The clear() calls must come after super().save() because many-to-many relations live in their own table keyed on this row’s primary key, which does not exist until the save has run.

class Article(*args, **kwargs)¶

Bases: Model

A single news article, pending or approved.

An article belongs either to a journalist working alone or to a publisher as an organisation, never both - so author and publisher are both nullable and clean() enforces the either/or rule.

Both foreign keys use on_delete=SET_NULL: a journalist leaving or a publisher being deleted must not take already-published articles with them. approved defaults to False, making publication an explicit editor decision.

clean()¶

Reject impossible ownership combinations.

bool(self.author_id) == bool(self.publisher_id) is true when both are set or neither is - precisely the invalid pair, since the rule is “exactly one owner”.

The test reads author_id, the raw key value, rather than author. Following the relation would issue a database query on every validation and would raise on an unsaved instance.

save(*args, **kwargs)¶

Validate before every write.

Django only runs full_clean() inside forms, never automatically on save(). Calling it here keeps the “exactly one owner” rule enforcing itself for objects created straight through the ORM or the API.

class Newsletter(*args, **kwargs)¶

Bases: Model

A collection of articles issued to subscribers.

author cascades, since an edition without its owner has no meaning, while articles is many-to-many so one article can feature in several newsletters and deleting an edition never deletes the articles inside it.

class ApprovedArticleLog(*args, **kwargs)¶

Bases: Model

An audit entry written each time an article is approved.

article_title is copied onto the log instead of being read through the relation, so the entry stays legible in the admin if the article is later renamed. The log cascades with its article, making it a record of current content rather than a permanent history.

API serializers¶

Serializers that define the shape of the News API’s JSON responses.

Each class converts a Django model instance to and from JSON for the REST endpoints, and controls which fields a client may write. The read_only_fields lists are the security boundary of the API: anything not listed there can be set by whoever calls the endpoint.

class UserSerializer(*args, **kwargs)¶

Bases: ModelSerializer

Public, read-only view of a user account.

Every field is read-only, so this serializer can expose a user’s role in a response without allowing a client to change it through the API.

class Meta¶

Bases: object

class UserRegistrationSerializer(*args, **kwargs)¶

Bases: ModelSerializer

Accepts new reader sign-ups and creates the account safely.

password is write-only, so it is never echoed back in a response, and is checked against Django’s password validators before saving.

Create the user with a hashed password and the default reader role.

Uses create_user, not create, so Django hashes the password; writing through create would store it in plain text.

Reject the submission if any chosen article is still unapproved.

This is the API’s only guarantee that unreviewed work cannot be published, so it is enforced here rather than relying on the form or view to filter the list first.

HTML views¶

Server-rendered HTML views for the Daily Brief website.

These function-based views power the pages a reader sees in a browser, while views.py supplies the JSON API. Where a page must behave identically to the API, it calls the API view instead of duplicating the logic, so the two cannot drift apart.

article_list(request)¶

Render every approved article.

select_related pulls each article’s author and publisher into the same query; without it the template would run an extra query per row.

article_detail(request, pk)¶

Render one approved article, or return a 404 if there is none.

The approval filter is part of the query rather than a check afterwards, so an unapproved article cannot be reached even by guessing its primary key.

article_create(request)¶

Let a journalist submit an article for editorial review.

The role check is done here as well as in the form, and author is taken from the logged-in session twice over - on form.instance and on the saved object - so a crafted POST cannot claim to be written by someone else.

pending_articles(request)¶

Show an editor the articles still waiting for a decision.

approve_article(request, pk)¶

Approve a pending article by delegating to the API view.

@require_POST matters: approving sends email to every subscriber, so a GET request must never trigger it. Without the decorator a browser prefetch, a link scanner or an image proxy could publish an article by loading the page.

newsletter_list(request)¶

Render every newsletter with its articles.

prefetch_related is used rather than select_related because articles is a many-to-many relation, which cannot be joined in a single query.

newsletter_create(request)¶

Let a journalist or editor assemble and save a newsletter.

commit=False saves the newsletter without its many-to-many articles, because the author must be set from the session before the row is written; save_m2m() then attaches the chosen articles afterwards. Omitting that second call would silently create a newsletter with no content.

This method should always be used rather than accessing self.queryset directly, as self.queryset gets evaluated only once, and those results are cached for all subsequent requests.

You may want to override this if you need to provide different querysets depending on the incoming request.

(Eg. return a list of items that is specific to the user)

Forms¶

Model forms used by the Daily Brief web interface.

Defines the forms that capture article submissions and newsletter creation. Keeping them separate from the views lets field layout and validation rules be read without also reading the request-handling logic.

class ArticleSubmissionForm(data=None, files=None, auto_id='id_%s', prefix=None, initial=None, error_class=<class 'django.forms.utils.ErrorList'>, label_suffix=None, empty_permitted=False, instance=None, use_required_attribute=None, renderer=None)¶

Bases: ModelForm

Form a journalist uses to submit an article for editorial review.

Only the title and body are editable here. Approval status and authorship are set by the view, so a submitter cannot mark their own work as approved.

Admin registration¶

Django admin registrations for the news app.

Declares which models administrators can manage through the built-in admin dashboard, and extends the default user edit form with the app’s own role field so an administrator can change someone’s role without editing the database directly.

class CustomUserAdmin(model, admin_site)¶

Bases: UserAdmin

Django’s user admin, extended with the news app’s role field.

fieldsets controls the edit form for an existing account and add_fieldsets the form used when creating one. Both append a “News App Details” section, because replacing the tuple outright would hide Django’s built-in username and password fields.

fieldsets = ((None, {'fields': ('username', 'password')}), ('Personal info', {'fields': ('first_name', 'last_name', 'email')}), ('Permissions', {'fields': ('is_active', 'is_staff', 'is_superuser', 'groups', 'user_permissions')}), ('Important dates', {'fields': ('last_login', 'date_joined')}), ('News App Details', {'fields': ('role',)}))¶
add_fieldsets = ((None, {'classes': ('wide',), 'fields': ('username', 'usable_password', 'password1', 'password2')}), ('News App Details', {'fields': ('role',)}))¶

Signals¶

Role synchronisation signal for the news app.

Listens for each User as it is saved and keeps that account’s Django group membership aligned with the role selected on the user model. This means permissions granted to a role group take effect without an administrator having to assign the group by hand.

sync_user_role_group(sender, instance, **kwargs)¶

Keep each account’s Django group aligned with its selected role.
